While the prose is thoughtful and well-crafted, the story relies on several well-worn college fiction tropes and character archetypes that border on cliché. These include the sensitive senior writer who mines his partner's private life for his own art (Carl), the pretentious and analytical graduate student who psychoanalyzes the protagonist (Martin), the cynical, oversized-sweater-wearing best friend who offers sharp commentary on everyone (Lizzy), and the quiet, observant foreign photographer who truly "sees" the protagonist without judgment (Johan). Furthermore, the overarching coming-of-age plot—a naive literature student navigating romantic entanglement and learning she must "meet herself first" rather than defining herself through others' opinions—is a very familiar narrative arc.
